findings.title: `isTeamAdminOrOwner` uses `&&` instead of `||`, blocking team admins from adding guests
findings.body: In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts` at lines 46-48, `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed as `(await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...))`. Because `isTeamAdmin` checks for `MembershipRole.ADMIN` and `isTeamOwner` checks for `MembershipRole.OWNER` (or equivalent mutually exclusive/distinct roles), requiring both to be true means a team admin who is not an owner (or vice versa) will evaluate to `false` and receive a `FORBIDDEN` error when trying to add guests to a team booking. This should use `||` instead of `&&`.

findings.title: Calendar event is updated using the caller's credentials instead of the booking organizer's
findings.body: In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts` at lines 158-165, `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)` and `new EventManager({ ...user, credentials })` use the currently logged-in caller (`ctx.user`) rather than the booking's organizer (`booking.user`). `addGuestsHandler` explicitly allows attendees and team admins/owners who are not the organizer to add guests (lines 46-56). When an attendee or team admin calls `addGuests`, `EventManager` will try to update the calendar event using the caller's credentials and user record instead of the organizer's, failing to update the organizer's calendar event.

findings.title: Duplicate emails in `input.guests` and case differences bypass deduplication and blacklisting
findings.body:
In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts` at lines 74-78, `uniqueGuests` only filters against existing `booking.attendees` and `blacklistedGuestEmails` using case-sensitive comparisons, and does not deduplicate `input.guests` itself:
1. If the tRPC endpoint is called directly with duplicate entries in `guests` (e.g. `["a@b.com", "a@b.com"]`), `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` in `addGuests.schema.ts` does not enforce uniqueness, so duplicate attendee rows will be created in the database and multiple emails sent.
2. `blacklistedGuestEmails` is lowercased on line 71, but `guest` is not lowercased before `blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)` or `guest === attendee.email`, so submitting `User@Example.com` bypasses both the blacklist and existing-attendee checks.
3. On line 168, `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` is passed the raw `guests` array instead of `uniqueGuests`, so if an existing attendee's email was included in `guests`, that existing attendee will receive `AttendeeScheduledEmail` instead of `AttendeeAddGuestsEmail`.

findings.title: `sendAddGuestsEmails` ignores event type `disableStandardEmails` metadata settings
findings.body: In `packages/emails/email-manager.ts` at lines 525-550, unlike `sendLocationChangeEmails`, `sendScheduledEmails`, and `sendRescheduledEmails`, `sendAddGuestsEmails` does not accept `eventTypeMetadata` or check `eventTypeDisableHostEmail(eventTypeMetadata)` / `eventTypeDisableAttendeeEmail(eventTypeMetadata)`. Event types configured to suppress standard host or attendee emails will still send emails whenever guests are added.
